etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English pilory, pillorie, from Old French pilori, pellori, which is either from Old Occitan espilori or Latin pīla (“pillar”).
senses: (chiefly historical) A framework on a post, with holes for the hands and head, used as a means of punishment and humiliation.
(transitive, figurative) To subject to humiliation, scorn, ridicule or abuse.
